{{Short description|German theoretical physicist}}
'''Jeroen van den Brink''' (born November 18, 1968) is a theoretical [[Condensed matter physics|condensed matter]] physicist, director at the [[Leibniz Institute for Solid State and Materials Research]], [[IFW Dresden]] and professor at the [[Dresden University of Technology]] in Germany. Van den Brink is known for contributions to the field of [[strongly correlated material]]s, in particular for proposals on [[magnetism|magnetic]] and orbital ordering,<ref name = Brink1999>{{cite journal |title =  Double-exchange via degenerate orbitals |author =  J. van den Brink and D. Khomskii|journal = [[Physical Review Letters]] |volume = 82|issue = 5|page = 1016 |year = 1999|arxiv = cond-mat/9810394 |bibcode = 1999PhRvL..82.1016V |doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.82.1016 |s2cid = 55977506}}</ref><ref name = Brink2006>{{cite journal |title =  Transition Metal Oxides: Travels in one dimension|author =  J. van den Brink |journal = [[Nature Materials]]|volume = 5|issue = 6|year = 2006 |pmid=16738674|bibcode = 2006NatMa...5..427V |doi = 10.1038/nmat1648 |pages =  427–8 |s2cid = 195293149 }}</ref>  mechanisms for [[Multiferroics|multiferroicity]]<ref name = Efremov2004>{{cite journal |title =  Bond- versus site-centred ordering and possible ferroelectricity in manganites|author = D.V. Efremov, J. van den Brink and D.I. Khomskii
|journal = [[Nature Materials]]|volume = 3|issue = 12|year = 2004 |pmid=15558036|bibcode = 2004NatMa...3..853E |doi = 10.1038/nmat1236 |pages =  853–6 |s2cid = 19521760
}}</ref> and the theory of [[RIXS|Resonant Inelastic X-Ray Scattering (RIXS)]].

He obtained a PhD from the [[University of Groningen]] in 1997 under the supervision of [[George Sawatzky|George A. Sawatzky]] and [[Daniel Khomskii]]. From 2002–2009, he was a professor of theoretical condensed matter physics working at [[Leiden University]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof. Dr. Jeroen van den Brink |url=https://www.ifw-dresden.de/ifw-institutes/itf/home/prof-dr-jeroen-van-den-brink/cv |access-date=2026-11-08 |website=www.ifw-dresden.de}}</ref> and in 2009 visiting professor at the
[[Stanford University|Stanford Institute for Materials and Energy Science]].
